sector_model: Medtech neurovascular and thrombectomy devices, pending cash-and-stock merger target (large): the price is anchored to the Boston Scientific offer, not standalone fundamentals; deal spread and regulatory risk are the model.
thesis: Penumbra (NYSE: PEN). Q3 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-10-29) read in part. Merger Agreement dated 2026-01-14: Boston Scientific to acquire PEN at 374 per share (10-Q wording; enterprise value about 14.5B; consideration mix not stated in the text read); closing expected early 2027 subject to regulatory approvals; termination fees 525.0M payable by PEN and 900.0M by Boston Scientific in specified cases. Close 320.60 (2026-11-18) vs 374 implies a gross spread of 16.7% (374/320.60 - 1), unusually wide for a deal expected within months, which signals market doubt about regulatory approval, financing or timing (cause not verified). Standalone: Q3 revenue 410.1M vs 354.7M (+15.6%); 9M 1,174.9M (+15.4%); 9M NI 109.7M vs 130.3M (-15.9%) as tax rate rose to 23.9% from 7.9%. TTM (USD): revenue 1,560.3M, NI 157.0M, OCF 261.0M, capex 60.8M, FCF 200.2M, SBC 58.4M. Market cap 320.60 x 39,414,385 shares (cover 2026-10-14) = 12.64B = 80.5x TTM NI, FCF yield 1.6%; cash 254.3M plus marketable investments 419.3M, no borrowings (finance leases 21.4M), total liabilities 441.6M. Standalone multiples are not a valuation basis while the offer exists.
counterthesis: If the deal fails, the stock may fall toward a standalone value: 80x trailing earnings and a 1.6% FCF yield assume sustained 15% growth and margin recovery, with the tax rate rising and 9M profit falling. The spread already prices some break risk; fees of 900M from the acquirer are not guaranteed relief. A researcher cannot add an edge on antitrust outcomes from filings alone. Duplicates medtech exposure often held through index funds.
invalidation: For a deal-spread view: invalidated by an antitrust second request or challenge, a financing change, a termination notice or an amended lower price. For a standalone view: growth below 10% or falling margins.
